name: CodeViewr code blocks diff
description:
1. You asked to eliminate space-heavy `alert` elements and replace them with compact single-line notices using small text, icons, and semantic colors.
2. I located `CodeViewer.vue` and converted four DaisyUI alert blocks into slim `flex` status strips (`px-2 py-1 rounded bg-{semantic}/10 text-xs`).
3. Each strip pairs a Font Awesome icon with a `<strong>` label so meaning is never conveyed by color alone (WCAG AA compliance).
4. Long content is preserved via `truncate` plus native `title` tooltips; the multi-line `changesetErrors` list became a count + first-error summary.
5. No JS logic, props, emits, or data changed—only template markup—and I provided the full file, a change summary table, accessibility checklist, and anti-patterns.

messages.content:
This one is gonna be complex, I think...
We need to add code blocks comparion/diff between messages.
Example: User adds a code block (with or without a valid file) and requests changes on that content.
The assistant generates changes, now we need to compare the new block with the block in the previous messages.
The diff is a feature of codeviewer component but currently only works againts project's files not other blocks.
Review, analyze and suggest the best way to have "code block diffs" so we can compare code blocks vs file and other versions of the code block in previous messages (only previous messages)

<!-- inside <script> computed: { ... } — add next to messageContent() -->
    messageContent() {
      return this.displayMessage.content
    },
    /**
     * All code blocks from the messages that precede this one in the chat
     * (newest first), used to diff this message's blocks against their
     * previous versions. See service/chat.collectCodeBlocksFromMessages.
     */
    previousCodeBlocks() {
      const messages = this.chat?.messages || []
      const currentId = this.message?.doc_id || this.message?.id
      const currentIndex = messages.findIndex(m => (m.doc_id || m.id) === currentId)
      if (currentIndex <= 0) return []

      const previousMessages = messages.slice(0, currentIndex).filter(m => !m.hide)
      return this.$service.chat.collectCodeBlocksFromMessages(previousMessages)
    },

baseFileChanged: false,

      actionFeedback: {

        save: false,
        patch: false

---

# The Plan — Ordered to Avoid Breaking Changes

## ✅ Required: 1 file only

| # | File | Why it's needed | Breaking risk |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | `src/components/CodeViewer.vue` | Reads `chat.messages` + `message`, finds the prior block **by file name**, feeds the existing `DiffViewer` a different baseline | **None** — fully additive & guarded |

Everything is **opt-in**: if there's no previous matching block, the "Compare" button simply doesn't render. Remove/comment the button later and the file behaves exactly like today.

---

✅ **Checkpoint:** Stream a message with two file-named code blocks across two turns → the second block shows **Compare**. Blocks without a file name show nothing.

messages.content:
A code block can appear in multiple messages before.
@DaisyUI The diff with previous messages must be a drop down allowing to select the previous message to compare.

Looking at this request, I need to transform the "Compare with previous version" single-toggle into a **dropdown that lists all previous message versions** so the user can pick which one to diff against. Here's what changes: **Plan:** 1. Replace `previousCodeBlock` (single, most-recent) with `previousCodeBlocks` (array of ALL prior versions across messages, newest first). 2. Add `selectedPreviousId` state + `selectedPreviousBlock` computed to derive the active comparison. 3. Swap the "Compare" button for a DaisyUI `dropdown` menu listing every prior version (user + relative time), plus a "File on disk" option to exit comparison. 4. Update selection methods (`selectPreviousVersion`, `clearPreviousDiff`) replacing `togglePreviousDiff`. ```vue src/components/CodeViewer.vue ``` ### Change Summary | Area | Before | After | |------|--------|-------| | `previousCodeBlock` (single) | Returned only the *most recent* prior match | `previousCodeBlocks` returns **all** prior matches (newest first) with `messageId`, `user`, `when` | | Selection state | Implicit (always newest) | New `selectedPreviousId` data property + `selectedPreviousBlock` computed | | Compare UI | Toggle `
Don't use "alert" elements, they occupy too much space, use single lines with small text, icons and colors are ok

## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking - **Core Requirements:** Replace the four DaisyUI `alert` blocks inside `CodeViewer.vue` with compact, single-line notification strips that use small text, a leading icon, and semantic color, without occupying multi-line vertical space. - **Strategic Approach:** 1. Keep the same `v-if` conditions so behavior is unchanged. 2. Convert each `alert` into a flex row: `flex items-center gap-1.5 px-2 py-1 rounded bg-{semantic}/10 text-{semantic} text-xs`. 3. Truncate long content with `truncate` and surface the full message via a native `title` tooltip (single-line layout preserved). 4. Handle the `changesetErrors` list (naturally multi-line) by showing a one-line summary + `title` tooltip listing all errors. - **Dependencies & Risks:** No JS logic, props, emits, or data touched. Only markup classes change. The parent container already adds `bg-error/40` when `isContentOutdated`, which continues to work. - **Target Files:** `src/components/CodeViewer.vue` (modify). ## 2. Minimum Changes Approach Single file, four isolated template blocks. All four `alert`-classed wrappers are replaced with compact inline strips. Everything else (script, methods, styles, other markup) is left untouched. ## 3. File changes ```vue src/components/CodeViewer.vue ``` ## 4. File Change Summary | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/CodeViewer.vue` | Modify | `isContentOutdated` banner | Replaced `alert alert-sm text-error` with a single-line strip: `flex items-center gap-1.5 px-2 py-1 rounded bg-error/10 text-error text-xs` + icon + `truncate`; full text moved to `title` tooltip. | | `src/components/CodeViewer.vue` | Modify | `isDangerousChange` banner | Replaced `alert alert-warning alert-sm` with a compact `bg-warning/10`/`text-warning` inline row; long inline `` label text so meaning isn't conveyed by color alone. - Error/info strips are static text (not interactive) so no focus ring is required; the `showPreviousDiff` close button is keyboard-reachable and has `aria-label="Exit comparison"`. - Truncated messages expose full content through the native `title` attribute; contrast relies on DaisyUI semantic tokens (`text-error`, `text-warning`, `text-info`) on `/{10}` tinted backgrounds — verify against your theme's WCAG AA tokens if a custom palette is used. ### Anti-Patterns Avoided - ❌ Full-width multi-line `alert` blocks that push the code viewport down. - ❌ Color-only status signaling (labels retained alongside icons/colors). - ❌ Removing content without a fallback (full text kept in tooltips).

history.summary:
1. You asked for a feature to diff code blocks against earlier versions of the same block in previous chat messages, not just against project files.
2. I analyzed the architecture: `ChatEntry` → `Document` → `Code` → `CodeViewer` → `DiffViewer`, where the existing diff only compares a block against the file on disk.
3. I proposed injecting a "reference baseline" (a previous message's block) into the content-agnostic `DiffViewer` rather than building a new diff engine.
4. The solution adds a new `utils/codeBlockDiff.js` matcher (path → filename → content/language similarity) plus `extractAllCodeBlocks` and `collectCodeBlocksFromMessages` to gather prior blocks newest-first.
5. It wires `previousBlocks` through `ChatEntry` → `Document` → `Code`, and adds a "Compare" mode + banner in `CodeViewer`, with all changes additive and optional-prop driven for safe rollback.

1. Goal: add code-block diffing so a code block can be compared against the same block from **previous messages**, not just against project files.
2. First proposal introduced new utils (`codeBlockDiff.js`, extractor changes, service method) with prop drilling through ChatEntry → Document → Code.
3. You requested simplification: reuse `CodeViewer`'s existing diff engine and map blocks by **file name** (` ```language filename `), skipping blocks without a file name.
4. Final solution touches **only `src/components/CodeViewer.vue`** — it resolves the previous block via `chat.messages` + `extractCodeBlocksFromMessage`, adds a "Compare" toggle, and feeds the existing `DiffViewer`.
5. Full `CodeViewer.vue` content was delivered, with `ChatEntry`/`Chat`/`ChatMessageList` confirmed to need no changes.

1. You want to add **code block diffs** so a block can be compared against its previous version in earlier messages (not just against project files).
2. Key discovery: `CodeViewer.vue` already has diff functionality **and** already receives `chat` + `message` props, so no new diff engine or prop drilling is needed.
3. Matching is done **by code block file name** (` ```language filename `); blocks without a file name are skipped.

5. All changes are **additive and guarded** (no previous match → no button), so existing file-diff behavior is unaffected; `ChatEntry.vue`, `Chat.vue`, `ChatMessageList.vue`, `Document.vue`, and `Code.vue` need **no changes**.

1. User requested changing the "Compare with previous version" feature in `CodeViewer.vue` from a single toggle button into a dropdown for selecting which prior message version to diff against.
